ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #12
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. went
   B. goed
   C. going
   D. goes

2. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.

3. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.

4. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. One main idea with supporting sentences
   B. Many unrelated topics with no link
   C. No full stops
   D. Only one word repeated

5. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.

6. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.

7. When practising Play: Structure and Setting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Play: Structure and Setting.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Play: Structure and Setting.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Play: Structure and Setting.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Play: Structure and Setting.

8. When practising Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.

9. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only a describing word
   C. Only a joining word
   D. Only an action

10. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.

11. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library
   B. where is the library
   C. Where is the Library
   D. Where is the library?

12. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. blue
   B. happiness
   C. run
   D. quickly

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 7.4.1 Intensive Reading: Play and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 7.5.1 The Writing Process and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Oral Poetry and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Interpretation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — went

2. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.

3. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.

4. A — One main idea with supporting sentences

5. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.

6. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.

7. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Play: Structure and Setting.

8. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.

9. A — A person, place, thing, or idea

10. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.

11. D — Where is the library?

12. C — run

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 7.4.1 Intensive Reading: Play; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 7.5.1 The Writing Process; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Oral Poetry; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Interpretation; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
